title: [CQ-M07] Turn on verified-local: starting a worker or QA agent runs it in a Moe VM
definitionOfDone: With executionProfile absent, legacy or observe, launching agents behaves exactly as today; regression tests cover the JetBrains launcher and both wrappers.
With verified-local and readiness met, JetBrains Start Agent for a worker or QA seat runs the CLI inside an owned VM via agent-lifecycle.mjs, and the host never runs that seat's agent CLI. Tested.
With verified-local and readiness not met, Start Agent refuses with a dialog naming each missing capability. No terminal, no VM and no host fallback. Tested.

assertExecutionProfileReady derives readiness from evidence: a passing certify report for this host's platform that matches the current provider version, image pin and supervisor pin, plus the other listed capabilities. Tests prove that no env var, setting, persisted label, caller argument, or report file inside the project or .moe/ satisfies it.
An agent job's changes reach the branch only through export and host admission, then the wrapper's landing. The job's VM is deleted on every exit path, through the owned ledger. Tested.
VS Code reaches parity with the JetBrains launch route and refusal.
Docs are updated: the executionProfile row in CONFIGURATION.md, 'Nothing here is active yet' in ARCHITECTURE.md Local Runner Isolation, and 'Certification is not activation' in CERTIFICATION.md.
One end-to-end task runs on a real VM on Windows and on Linux, run by the human or the governor (not a seat), with the outcome recorded as a task comment.
Daemon npm test, ./gradlew test and node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs pass, run in a git-archive snapshot and not in place in the shared checkout.
taskRails: Never let an env var, setting, persisted label, caller argument or project-supplied file grant verified-local.
Never fall back to running the agent CLI on the host when the VM path fails; refuse instead.
Legacy, the default, stays byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior.
No seat runs Multipass. Real-VM runs belong to the human or the governor.
Do not loosen guest readiness, the certified-provider.json pins or guest-supervisor.py's guarantees.
The open design decisions (VM per job or per seat, the concurrency cap, WSL agent mode, report trust) go to the human before submit_plan.

implementationPlan.description:
Build the plugin from the activated tree, post the real-VM runbook to the governor, and park the row for the human/governor runs. This covers DoD 8 and extras 2-3 of comment-8bf3a7e4. No repo file changes.

1. PLUGIN. Hold the jetbrains-gradle lease for the whole build (moe.acquire_resource jetbrains-gradle; mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease).
   - Snapshot the task worktree's files into a fresh `mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/m07fp-XXXXXX` dir, exactly as checkRefs[1] does (git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -- . ':!.moe' | tar).
   - Run Windows npm ci and npm run build in packages/moe-daemon and in packages/moe-proxy, then `.\gradlew.bat buildPlugin` through cmd.exe.
   - Record the zip's Windows path and sha256.
   - Error handling: a failed npm or Gradle step stops the build. The lease is released on every path, success or failure. The failure goes into the step note with its exit code and log tail, and no runbook is posted for a tree that did not build.
2. RUNBOOK. Post ONE comment on this row addressed to @governor-e6142a94. Build it from the landed docs (CERTIFICATION.md's activation section from CQ-M07v1, the TROUBLESHOOTING rows from CQ-M07v2) and the landed code. Every command must be exact and copy-pasteable, per host:
   (a) Install the zip (path and sha256) in JetBrains on the Windows host, and restart so a plugin-installed daemon serves the scratch project. protected-host-control-plane needs the daemon installed outside the project.
   (b) On Windows (native PowerShell) and on Linux: the certify command; the expected report file under <OS account home>/.moe/certification/ and its sha256; then the exact scripts/moe-call.sh line for moe.get_execution_readiness, to see what is still missing.
   (c) VM credentials: `accounts vm-token <id>` for every rotation account (or the Accounts tab's Set VM token...). For codex seats, OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY in the operator's environment.
   (d) A scratch project, never the moes board:
       - git init, a tiny npm package with one passing test and its package-lock.json, and .moe created by the plugin;
       - settings deliveryPolicy local-branch, worktreeMode 'on', qualityGate 'npm test';
       - executionProfile verified-local through the recorded settings path (UPDATE_SETTINGS over /ws; read WebSocketServer.ts's handler and give the exact one-liner);
       - checkEnvironments set by hand in .moe/project.json, from the environment id the first gate refusal prints (CQ-M07w plus CQ-M07r/s).
   (e) The runs:
       - Legacy first: with executionProfile absent, one task goes architect -> worker -> QA -> landed DONE.
       - Then verified-local: one task whose plan declares executionContract.requiredChecks for 'npm test' with configs ['package-lock.json']. Use Start Agent for worker and QA. On Windows the seats run native PowerShell even with WSL agent mode on; on Linux they run moe-agent.sh.
       - List the expected evidence at each stage, with the exact line or field: seat-start's {ok:true, instance}; the claim carrying executionRoute 'vm'; the admitted tree on moe/task/<id>; the check-dispatch report with every owed check passed; the completion commit on the target; the delivery receipt; qa_approve -> DONE; seat-stop's vm 'deleted'; vm-control status listing no owned VM afterwards.
   (f) Outcomes: one comment per host on this row (Windows, Linux). Each gives the plugin sha256, the report sha256, the (e) evidence, any failing code, and the human's promotion decision (for example: legacy stays the default, and verified-local is opt-in on certified hosts).
   (g) Rollback: executionProfile back to legacy through the same path. Tasks with a stored verified-local snapshot stay strict (CONFIGURATION.md).
3. complete_step this step. Then call moe.report_blocked on this row:
   - reason: "waiting for the human/governor real-VM runs of <runbook comment id> (DoD 8; comment-8bf3a7e4 extras 2-3)";
   - blockedOnTaskIds [];
   - needsFrom governor-e6142a94.
   End the session. A later session resumes at step 3 once the governor unblocks the row.

Record the real-VM outcomes and the promotion decision. Resume here once the governor has unblocked the row, and read every outcome comment posted on it since the step-2 runbook.

IF EITHER HOST'S RUN FAILED: file one bug row per distinct failure in this epic (moe.create_task with the evidence lines and the failing code). Then call moe.report_blocked on this row, with blockedOnTaskIds naming those rows and a reason asking the governor to re-run that host after they land. End the session. Never record a promotion on a failed run.

- Platform support: the linux x64 and win32 x64 rows gain the end-to-end outcome and its comment ids; the 'any platform, verified-local enabled' and 'this host' rows are restated from the runs; darwin x64 and arm64 stay unsupported (not certified);

(1) Producer/consumer drift:

DESIGN DECISIONS (human, 2026-11-01, architect REPL). Full text: mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation.
1. VM per SEAT, not per job. Each worker/QA seat gets one owned VM, reused for every job. Between jobs: verified sweep, a NEW root-only supervisor `reset` (materialize refuses an existing workspace), then a fresh materialize. The human accepted /tmp residue across one seat's tasks. The VM is deleted through the owned ledger when the seat exits; cleanup reclaims a crashed seat's VM once the seat is proven gone.
2. Cap derived from host size, host-wide: max(1, min(floor(CPUs/2), floor((RAM-8 GiB)/4 GiB))) agent VMs. Check VMs keep their own dispatch. A seat over the cap waits before claiming, never falls back to the host.
3. WSL mode: under verified-local, worker/QA seats launch natively on Windows (PowerShell + Windows Multipass) whatever the WSL toggle; architect/governor keep WSL; moe-agent.sh refuses verified-local inside WSL.
4. Report trust: host store, live match. Certify files certified reports in <OS account home>/.moe/certification/ (no env override, symlinks refused, nothing inside the project or .moe/). The daemon accepts only native + certified + this host's platform/arch + the LIVE Multipass version + the shipped image and supervisor pins.
5. VM credentials: per-account tokens minted by the accounts CLI into an owner-only store; rotation stays on. codex uses OPENAI_API_KEY/CODEX_API_KEY. gemini/grok are refused under verified-local.
Accepted consequence: the reset mode moves R13's supervisor pin (3a19f3bf), so it is sequenced right after task-fd196d13 and ONE operator re-certify covers both.

@architect-30d804be The fd196d13 transport design is ruled **APPROVED** (comment-d954b3df), and **Gate 0 passed on both real hosts** (comment-2566639b Windows, comment-888759e9 Linux). Your BACKLOG slices gated on that ruling (e, f, g, h, i, j, m, n) are clear to promote and plan at your pace. What the ruling means for them:
1. **Transport.** Every stdin or bulk stream goes over OpenSSH through guest-ssh.mjs (R14a `sshStreamArgv`) and R14d1/d2/d3's stream runners: materialize, export, verify, the install modes, bridge and check sessions. `multipass exec` stays only for stdin-less queries capped at 64 KiB.
   - M07f's `reset` and M07j's seat job run (materialize, bridge session, export) must reuse that route. Never exec stdio.
   - Your reset is a new supervisor mode, so add it to R14a's frozen `SUPERVISOR_MODES` in the same slice that adds it to guest-supervisor.py main(). The forced command passes any one word, and main()'s allowlist is the gate.
2. **Key custody.** Per-VM SSH keys live in `~/.moe/guest-ssh/<name>.{key,known_hosts}`, not runner-keys (R14a comment-f4d90818). M07g's seat-ledger cleanup must unlink both files when it deletes the VM, the same way R14c's purgeOwned does, and only once the VM is verified absent.
3. **Your stores stay separate.** The certification store (`<home>/.moe/certification/`) and M07k's per-account VM token store must each be their own owner-only directory. Not runner-keys, not guest-ssh, nothing under the project or .moe/.
4. **Pin and certify order.** Per the human's decision, M07f moves the 3a19f3bf pin and one re-certify covers fd196d13 plus M07f. I'll also run an **unrecorded early-signal certify** right after fd196d13 lands, so transport problems surface before M07f. Only the post-M07f run is recorded on R13.
5. **File order.** M07j (and any slice that edits snapshot-transfer.mjs, guest-session.mjs or guest-ssh.mjs) is already behind fd196d13, which depends on every R14 slice. Keep it that way. M07f's guest-supervisor.py edit is free of R14, since no R14 slice touches the supervisor.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: No runtime change. acceptanceCriteria: verifiedLocalActivation.acceptance.test.ts walks one verified-local task, plan -> marked claim -> complete -> candidate -> /runner dispatch and observation -> landed finalize -> receipt -> marked QA claim -> qa_approve, to DONE. It holds readiness READY only through readinessHolder.refreshReadiness, and each one-defect variant is refused with its exact code.
A verified-local consumer of that task is claimable once it is DONE, and stays claimable after it is ARCHIVED through the receipt. A twin with no receipt is withheld with delivery-receipt.

No worker or QA seat falls back to the host under verified-local.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Plan this row as one big activation implementation: rejected. The remaining functional gaps are split into CQ-M07r/s (the check-VM gate at L6 in sh/ps1), CQ-M07t (worktree delivery receipts), CQ-M07w (check-dispatch names the unapproved environment id), CQ-M07u (two QA test gaps) and CQ-M07v1/v2 (the DoD 7 docs). This row stays acceptance-only, and depends on all of them plus the open M07 bug rows bbd7ad2d and 1dfec7a4.
2. A real-daemon wrapper e2e under verified-local with fakes: impossible. No env var, setting or file may grant readiness (rail 1), and readiness needs a live Multipass probe. The wrapper side is proven by the slices' postflight-vm-route rows; the daemon side by this row's acceptance test; the whole thing by the real-VM run.
3. The real-board verified-local trial on the moes board itself: rejected. It would make every moes task strict, and every moes seat would need a VM. Use a scratch project.
4. Rail 6 (open design decisions to the human before submit_plan) is already met: comment-6af90ea8 and mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation (governor comment-737bdb9d). This plan re-asks nothing. The new choice made here (owed checks run at the worktree completion's L6 through check-dispatch.mjs, so the host never runs candidate code) follows from the task's own objective: 'required checks run in their own check VMs'.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Readiness is fully wired (CQ-M07a-d). It needs five things: a plugin-installed daemon outside the project (protected-host-control-plane); a runner key outside the project (authenticated-runner-evidence); a host-store certification report matching the live Multipass version and the image and supervisor pins (both isolation capabilities); and deliveryPolicy 'local-branch' (revision-bound-local-delivery).
- The moes dev daemon runs from packages/moe-daemon/dist inside the project, so this repo can never be verified-local ready. That is fine.
- Before CQ-M07r/s, nothing produced an authenticated CheckRun, so every verified-local qa_approve was refused, and the worktree L6 ran the qualityGate on the host on candidate bytes.
- Before CQ-M07t, the worktree journal had no candidateId and no receipt was ever sent.
- check-dispatch's owedChecks owes the qualityGate only for everyTask or epic-final scope, and needs every owed check declared in requiredChecks with a dependency choice. So a verified-local plan must declare requiredChecks (CQ-M07v1 documents it in the architect reference).
planningNotes.risks:
